London AdvancedAbout this tool
Charity Shops Map · methodology

A practical map for better second-hand browsing.

London’s charity shops can be useful visitor destinations: local, affordable and less predictable than standard retail. This tool turns a researched branch list into a location-first map.

It identifies specialist formats rather than treating every shop as interchangeable—particularly Oxfam bookshops, children’s shops, vintage boutiques and furniture branches.

Coverage
  • 245 shops
  • 12 charity organisations
  • Focus on TfL zones 1–4
  • Specialisms and available hours
How it works

Choose a place, then narrow the map.

  1. 01

    Locate

    Use your position or enter a station, street or landmark.

  2. 02

    Set distance

    Choose a radius from 200 metres to 1 kilometre.

  3. 03

    Filter

    Select specialist stock and one or more charities.

  4. 04

    Confirm

    Check the linked source before making a special journey.

What is included

A deliberately maintainable list.

Major London networks and relevant specialist chains are included where a retail branch falls mainly within TfL zones 1–4. Donation banks and non-retail collection points are excluded.

What to know

Stock and hours are not live.

Charity retail changes quickly. Coordinates use branch postcodes or address geocoding; they are suitable for nearby discovery but the linked directions and official source remain authoritative.

Common questions

Before using a result.

Does every shop sell the same things?

No. The map highlights bookshops, children’s shops, furniture branches and curated fashion where the source identifies them.

Are the opening hours live?

No. They are source-checked reference hours and can change temporarily.

Why only a 1 km radius?

The tool is designed for useful nearby detours on foot, not as a replacement for each charity’s national shop finder.
